stop_detail: SPADE deterministically extracts a build/test dependency graph (components, aggregators, runners, tests, packages) from CMake File API + CTest metadata (or manual construction for other build systems) and injects the full RIG as JSON into the agent's context at the start of the session as the 'authoritative' description of repo structure (Secs. III-IV).
threats_to_datum: 7 of 8 evaluation repositories are synthetic (only MetaFFI is real-world); small sample (8 repos x 30 questions) limits generalizability; three commercial agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) tested but no standard SE benchmark used. Full text retrieved via arXiv HTML.

demote_reason: Full text confirms this paper is about general LLM prompt compression for isolated, single-problem prompts (HumanEval, MBPP, HumanEval+, MultiPL-E function-level code problems vs. GSM8K/MATH/ARC/MMLU-STEM math-reasoning problems), comparing why code tolerates compression better than chain-of-thought math reasoning. There is no repository, codebase, multi-file, or cross-file structure of any kind -- no repo-map, dependency graph, or retrieval over a codebase is involved. It is a prompt-compression/perplexity study with no cross-file structural context-budget concern, so it falls outside the review's repository-level code-context-engineering scope.

confound_note: The manipulated variable is content freshness (current-commit vs. parent-commit helper signature) not representation or mechanism; retrieval itself is oracle-controlled/hand-assigned rather than an automatic embedding or similarity system, and prompts are neutralized to hide commit timestamps and expected signatures so only staleness is isolated.
stop_detail: A diagnostic harness manually substitutes current- vs. stale- (parent-commit) repository helper-function signatures as 'retrieved' context under five conditions (current-only, stale-only, no-retrieval, two mixed orders) to isolate whether stale retrieved context actively induces incompatible completions rather than acting as harmless noise (Methods).
threats_to_datum: Very small curated sample (n=17) restricted to argument-signature changes only (excludes renames/removals/larger temporal gaps), across just 5 mature Python libraries; retrieval is oracle-controlled rather than a real embedding-based RAG pipeline, limiting ecological validity of the diagnosed effect.
